title: Pirate Ship: goods on the skill trees (proposed)
status: Rex's splits of 2026-10-28 applied (Farming group; Cooking into Milling, Baking, Butchering, Preserving, Dairying, Waxworking; Tanning apart); placements still proposed

bands.name: Novice
bands.period: no trade grade; a labourer or a 'landsman' at sea (the sea grades date from 1652)

bands.name: Apprentice
bands.period: the guild grade: bound seven years, usually from 14 to 21 (Statute of Artificers; secondary summaries)

bands.name: Journeyman
bands.period: the guild grade: out of his time, free of the company, works for day wages (Campbell 1747)

bands.name: Expert
bands.period: no guild grade; the nearest is the 'able seaman', at least five years at sea (TNA). 'Head boiler' appears only in 1750s Jamaica, later than the period

bands.name: Master
bands.period: the guild grade: keeps a shop and apprentices; liveryman above it

flags.offMap: made outside the game's Caribbean in this period (Europe, Asia, Africa, the Spanish mainland); the skill tree says where it would sit if a town ever makes it
flags.input: needs a good from another skill (the chain the economy follows)
flags.gate: needs another skill at some level to reach the place (Swimming for depth); that skill makes nothing
flags.unsourced: Rex's addition with no period source found; a design good, not a historical record

groups.name: Gathering
groups.note: Skills that take goods from land and sea. Raw goods come from here. Swimming is a gate for depth, not a goods skill.

skills.name: Farming
skills.covers: planting, harvest, curing and packing crops; the dye plants and flowers as crops
skills.why: Crop cultivation only (Rex, 2026-10-28). Livestock, salt, dye-making and perfume have skills of their own.

items.name: Pease
items.note: a field crop any hand could grow and pick

items.name: Grain for meal and flour
items.note: planting and reaping; milling is Cooking

items.name: Cotton wool
items.note: picking and ginning before bagging (C81)

items.name: Ginger
items.note: the root is scraped so it stays white and does not sprout (L)

items.name: Tobacco, grown
items.note: topping and suckering the plant; the cure is the harder part

items.name: Cacao, grown
items.note: the tree; Jamaica's crops failed to a 'blast' (PT)

items.name: Sugar cane
items.note: planting, cutting and carting to the mill within a day of cutting (L); the boiling is Sugar boiling

items.name: Rice
items.note: wet-field rice took skill the Carolina planters bought from West Africa (SCR)

items.name: Tobacco, cured and packed
items.note: curing, prizing into the hogshead to at least 800 lb (VA30)

items.name: Pimento
items.note: picked green and sun-dried, kept from the dew (EB78)

items.name: Cacao, sweated and dried
items.note: sweated under plantain leaves, three or four weeks' sun (PT)

items.name: Indigo plant (grown and cut)
items.note: the crop; the vats are Dye Making

items.name: Nopal and cochineal (reared)
items.note: the insect reared on the cactus in Oaxaca (COC); the dye is Dye Making

items.name: Aromatic flowers and herbs
items.note: Rex's addition: a crop for Perfumery. No period Caribbean source; marked unsourced

skills.name: Animal Husbandry
skills.covers: breeding, feeding and keeping livestock; milk, wool, farm hides
skills.why: Split from Farming (Rex, 2026-10-28): keeping animals is its own expertise. Wild cattle and hogs stay with Hunting.

items.name: Horses
items.note: bred in New England and shipped at about £12 each (PY)

items.name: Cattle and hogs (farm)
items.note: the meat for Cooking's salt beef and pork

items.name: Milk
items.note: for Cooking's cheese and butter

items.name: Wool
items.note: English sheep; no Caribbean flock in the sources

items.name: Turtle crawls (kept live)
items.note: penned at Port Royal until sold (D); catching them is Fishing

skills.name: Marine Gathering
skills.covers: the shore and the shallows: salt pans, shells, pearls, seaweed
skills.why: Split from Farming (Rex, 2026-10-28). Pearls sit here with a Swimming gate for the depth, not a skill of their own.

items.name: Salt (raked)
items.note: sun does the work; raking the pans was ordinary labour (D, TC)

items.name: Pearls (dived)
items.note: the Rancheria banks; needs Swimming for the depth (E)

items.name: Tortoise shell
items.note: the hawksbill's plates (method open)

items.name: Cowries and shells
items.note: Maldives shells, a currency (UWF)

items.name: Seaweed
items.note: Rex's addition; no period trade in the sources, marked unsourced

skills.name: Hunting
skills.covers: tracking and killing wild cattle, hogs, deer; the carcass
skills.why: Obtaining the animal only (Rex, 2026-10-28). Skinning is Butchering, curing is Preserving, leather is Tanning. A hunter with low Butchering wastes the carcass.

items.name: Wild cattle and hog carcasses
items.note: Hispaniola's wild herds (E2)

items.name: Deer carcasses
items.note: Carolina's trade with the Indian nations (CCR)

items.name: Ivory
items.note: 'Elephant's Teeth' from the Guinea coast (J)

skills.name: Fishing
skills.covers: the catch; turtling at sea
skills.why: Already a skill with its own minigame. Turtling is netting at sea from sloops (D), so it stays here; shells and pearls are Marine Gathering.

items.name: Fresh fish
items.note: the minigame's catch

items.name: Turtle, live
items.note: netted at the Caymans and kept alive in crawls at Port Royal (D, HA)

skills.name: Woodcutting
skills.covers: felling, riving and squaring timber; the dyewood camps; tar, pitch and turpentine from the pine woods
skills.why: Logwood, lumber and naval stores all came out of the woods. Tar burning is folded in: the kilns stood in the forest and the same hands worked them (SCN).

items.name: Lumber (felled)
items.note: felling and hauling; any hand with an axe

items.name: Logwood
items.note: cut and chipped at the Campeche camps, sold at £5 a ton in goods (DV)

items.name: Staves and hoops (rived)
items.note: riving stave bolts for the cooper; Connecticut's cargo to Barbados (CT)

items.name: Shingles
items.note: rived and shaved; late evidence only (CTH)

items.name: Other dyewoods, lignum vitae
items.note: as logwood; fustic and brazeletto in the 1681 return (C81)

items.name: Tar, pitch, turpentine
items.note: the kiln burn takes judgement; 40,000 barrels a year by 1720 (SCN)

items.name: Mahogany
items.note: choosing, felling and squaring the great logs; 'bulky and relatively light' (MH)

skills.name: Mining
skills.covers: ore, the furnace and the forge that makes bar metal; silver refining
skills.why: Smelting sits here with the mine, not with the smith: the smith buys bar iron. Nearly all of it is off-map in this period (Spanish silver, Swedish and Bilbao iron).

items.name: Ore and lead
items.note: lead for shot; no Caribbean mine in the sources

items.name: Bar iron
items.note: £16 10s–£18 a ton in London (TR); 'voyage iron' to Africa (JS)

items.name: Brass, pewter, steel
items.note: alloying and steeling; European works

items.name: Silver
items.note: Potosí to Portobelo; refining with mercury (WHF)

items.name: Gold and gold dust
items.note: Brazil and the Guinea coast; washing dust takes less than refining silver

groups.name: Crafting
groups.note: Skills that turn raw goods into made ones. Each item names the good it needs.

skills.name: Cooking
skills.covers: meals and dishes; the galley; chocolate
skills.why: Meals only (Rex, 2026-10-28). Milling, Baking, Butchering, Preserving, Dairying and Waxworking are skills of their own.

items.name: Lime juice
items.note: pressed and casked; 1,512 gallons to London in one month (C81)

items.name: Salmagundi and the hot meal
items.note: the one hot meal from the galley (DUTIES); not a traded good

items.name: Chocolate
items.note: roasting and grinding the nut; a Spanish taste first

skills.name: Milling
skills.covers: grinding grain to flour and meal; the sugar mill is Sugar boiling
skills.why: Its own skill (Rex, 2026-10-28). New York guarded its flour's name with a bolting monopoly (VR).

items.name: Meal (coarse)
items.note: 'Barrels of meale close put up' (L)

items.name: Oatmeal
items.note: Roberts took '10 Casks of Oatmeal' (J)

items.name: Flour (bolted)
items.note: bolted fine; 196 lb to the barrel (FL)

skills.name: Baking
skills.covers: bread and ship's biscuit
skills.why: Its own skill (Rex, 2026-10-28). Large quantities of biscuit were baked in the Connecticut Valley and Philadelphia for the islands (PH).

items.name: Bread
items.note: daily bread; not a cargo

items.name: Ship's biscuit
items.note: baked hard, twice; 16s a hundredweight (PY); well baked, it keeps for years (SV)

skills.name: Butchering
skills.covers: skinning and dividing a carcass: meat, raw hide, fat, bone
skills.why: Its own skill (Rex, 2026-10-28): obtaining the animal is Hunting or Animal Husbandry; the carcass is this. Raw hides come from here.

items.name: Fresh meat
items.note: for the galley and for Preserving

items.name: Raw hides
items.note: flaying clean; 'cow hides 69 ... buff hides 768' to London (C81)

items.name: Tallow (rendered)
items.note: the fat rendered; sold with the hides (E2)

items.name: Deerskins (raw)
items.note: a clean skin is worth more; 'Skinns' from Carolina (CCR)

skills.name: Preserving
skills.covers: salting, smoking, drying: meat and fish that keep at sea
skills.why: Its own skill (Rex, 2026-10-28). The boucaniers' smoking frame and the salt-fish flakes are the same expertise: keeping food.

items.name: Salt fish
items.note: split, salted and dried; the poor grade went to the islands (HV)

items.name: Boucan (smoked meat)
items.note: hardened with smoke for sea voyages (E2)

items.name: Salt beef and pork
items.note: cut, brined and packed tight in barrel; a short barrel was noticed (PY)

items.name: Salted boar
items.note: 'salt it, and sell it so to the planters' (E2)

skills.name: Dairying
skills.covers: butter and cheese from milk
skills.why: Its own skill (Rex, 2026-10-28). Nearly all of it was off-map: Ligon says butter and cheese from England or Holland often spoil on the way (L).

items.name: Butter
items.note: in firkins; weight open (ML)

items.name: Cheese
items.note: 'a hundred-weight of Gloucester cheese' to Virginia (BR)

skills.name: Waxworking
skills.covers: candles first, then wax seals, moulded and ceremonial candles, wax portraits and figures
skills.why: Rex's skill (2026-10-28), renamed from Candlemaking so it has a ladder to Master. Tallow candles are sourced (L); beeswax and wax sculpture were real European trades but nothing in the period Caribbean sources, so those tiers are marked unsourced. Wax sculpture was an artist's trade, not the top of the chandler's; joining them is a design choice.

items.name: Tallow candles
items.note: dipped; they fuse in the heat (L)

items.name: Wax seals
items.note: sealing wax for letters; no Caribbean source

items.name: Beeswax candles
items.note: cleaner burning, for church and the cabin; beeswax supply in the Caribbean open

items.name: Moulded and altar candles
items.note: consistent sizes, ceremonial forms

items.name: Wax portraits and anatomical models
items.note: a European art of the period; unsourced here

items.name: Lifelike wax figures
items.note: the INFP's signature work (story: brothel, wax figures); a design good

skills.name: Tanning
skills.covers: raw hide to leather
skills.why: Kept apart from Butchering (Rex, 2026-10-28): a butcher skins, a tanner makes leather. Leatherworking (goods made from leather) is not a skill yet; open.

items.name: Dressed deerskin
items.note: the Carolina export went raw or half-dressed (open)

items.name: Tanned leather
items.note: bark pits take months; no Caribbean tannery in the sources, so off-map in practice

skills.name: Sugar boiling
skills.covers: the mill and the boiling house: molasses, muscovado, clayed sugar, loaf sugar
skills.why: The biggest cash crop. Ligon's boiler judges when to strike the sugar by eye and hand; a head boiler was the most valued man on a plantation. One-off nowhere: every sugar island needs it.

items.name: Molasses
items.note: what drains from the pots; the apprentice's share of the work (L)

items.name: Muscovado sugar
items.note: boiling through the coppers and striking; 3d a pound on Barbados (L)

items.name: Clayed (white) sugar
items.note: claying the pot so the molasses drains out; 20d a pound in London (L)

items.name: Loaf sugar
items.note: refined in Bristol and London cone moulds (DB1)

skills.name: Dye Making
skills.covers: the vats and the dye bath: indigo, annatto, cochineal; dyeing cloth
skills.why: Its own trade (Rex, 2026-10-28): extraction, fermentation, mordants and colour. Farming grows the plant, Dye Making makes the dye and colours the cloth.

items.name: Annatto dye
items.note: seed pulp worked to a paste (D)

items.name: Indigo dye
items.note: steeping, beating and judging the cut (C88, D)

items.name: Cochineal dye
items.note: killing and drying the insect; 18–45s a pound in London (TR)

items.name: Dyed cloth
items.note: the dye bath with a mordant; needs a dye from this tree too

skills.name: Distilling
skills.covers: the still and the brewhouse: rum, aqua vitae, brandy; beer and wine folded in
skills.why: Rex's own example. Brewing and winemaking are folded in as one-offs: no Caribbean town made wine or much beer in the sources, so they sit here off-map.

items.name: Beer
items.note: 'good English Beer' shipped out (L)

items.name: Aqua vitae (kill-devil)
items.note: the rough first spirit from the skimmings (L)

items.name: Rum
items.note: half a crown a gallon on Barbados (L); cask size open (1j)

items.name: Wine
items.note: Madeira, Fayal, Canary, claret: £8 a pipe at Jamestown (CSP)

items.name: Brandy
items.note: distilled wine; thirty casks in one prize (J)

skills.name: Perfumery
skills.covers: aromatic extraction, blending, fixing a scent
skills.why: Rex's addition (2026-10-28), kept apart from Distilling: a rum distiller is not a perfumer. No Caribbean perfume trade in the period sources; the goods are marked unsourced.

items.name: Fragrant oils and waters
items.note: unsourced for the Caribbean; a cultural good if one region prizes it

items.name: Perfume
items.note: unsourced; the finished luxury

skills.name: Smithing
skills.covers: the forge: nails, hoops, tools, blades, shot; gunsmithing at the top
skills.why: Already a skill. Gunsmithing is folded in as its top tier rather than a skill of its own. The great guns stay off-map: a foundry, not a forge.

items.name: Nails
items.note: 6d a pound retail (TR); the first thing an apprentice makes

items.name: Shot (cast lead)
items.note: 1,281 lead shot in one QAR lab batch (QAR)

items.name: Iron hoops
items.note: for the cooper; wooden hoops were the cheaper kind

items.name: Tools: hoes, axes, knives
items.note: 'nails, hoes, and axes' to Virginia (BR)

items.name: Small wares: pins, needles, combs
items.note: Bonnet took 'a few Combs, Pins and Needles' (J)

items.name: Manillas
items.note: brass currency for the Africa trade; 600 on the Whydah (WBUR)

items.name: Swords and cutlasses
items.note: steel blades; 'Swords, knives' shipped to Barbados (L)

items.name: Muskets and pistols
items.note: gunsmithing: lock, stock and barrel

items.name: Great guns (cannon)
items.note: cast at a foundry; 29 located on the QAR wreck (QAR)

skills.name: Carpentry
skills.covers: sawn timber and joinery; the ship's repairs (DUTIES)
skills.why: Already a skill, mostly for repairs. Its goods are few: the raw timber comes from Woodcutting and casks are Cooperage.

items.name: Planks and boards (sawn)
items.note: the saw pit

items.name: Mahogany, worked
items.note: joinery; the 1720s furniture trade (MH)

skills.name: Cooperage
skills.covers: casks: slack (dry) work for flour and sugar, tight (wet) work for rum, molasses and wine
skills.why: Already a skill, and the trade had a real ladder: a slack cooper made dry casks, a tight cooper the harder wet ones. About half the goods travel in its casks (3b).

items.name: Staves and heads, dressed
items.note: jointing and hollowing the staves

items.name: Slack casks (barrel, hogshead for dry goods)
items.note: flour barrels, sugar hogsheads; 196 lb of flour to the barrel (FL)

items.name: Tight casks (rum, molasses, wine)
items.note: must hold liquid; a leaking cask loses the rum (DUTIES)

skills.name: Weaving
skills.covers: spinning and weaving; rope; tailoring
skills.why: Cloth, canvas and cordage were the naval stores pirates took most (Part 2). Ropemaking and tailoring are folded in as one-offs. Nearly all of it is off-map: the colonies imported cloth (L, BR).

items.name: Cordage and cable
items.note: the ropewalk; 'two Cables, and several Coils of Rope' taken (J)

items.name: Coarse linen (dowlas, osnaburg)
items.note: 1s 5d–1s 8d an ell (TR); slaves' and servants' cloth

items.name: Clothing
items.note: tailoring folded in; a shirt at 2s 6d (CSP)

items.name: Sailcloth and canvas
items.note: the sailmaker sews it; the weaver makes it

items.name: Woollens (broadcloth, duffels)
items.note: 10s–23s 6d a yard (TR); duffels for the Indian trade (CSP)

items.name: Fine linen (holland)
items.note: 2s 4d–2s 8d a yard (TR)

items.name: Silk, chintz, muslin
items.note: Asian looms; chintzes in a French prize (J)

skills.name: Surgery and medicine
skills.covers: the apothecary's medicines and the surgeon's chest
skills.why: Already a skill. Apothecary work is folded in: a town with a surgeon has its medicines from the same hands.

items.name: Simple medicines
items.note: the apothecary's stock; 'some of the Ship's Medicines' pressed (J)

items.name: Surgeon's chest and instruments
items.note: £300–400 at Charleston (J); 200–250 pieces of eight as a fixed share (E)

noTree.name: Gunpowder
noTree.note: powder mills were a trade of their own in Europe; nothing in the sources makes it in the Caribbean. Imported only, or Smithing master if Rex wants a town to make it

noTree.name: Voyage iron
noTree.note: the same bar iron as Mining: Bar iron, sold as currency on the African coast

noTree.name: Africa trade cargo
noTree.note: a mix of the goods above, not a good

bandsSource: research-trade-grades.md (shared notes folder): guild ladder, sea ranks, Ligon's overseers and tradesmen; 'novice' and 'expert' found as no grade
